question: Under profile enhanced at main a25c82f, where a connection that fails at its class width is retried with every trace at 300 um (router.neck_width_um = 300, Java's necked retry), does Q17.3's widen-back after that retry, or Q17.2's bounded-neck stage (the neck only within D of a pin) with the widen-back, keep the KiCad-unconnected total within N02's totals rule (accept no-regress) with no new clearance, width, via-in-pad or power-layer-trace breach, and either beat the retry on unconnected by more than the set's noise or ship less copper under the Board Setup width of the wide classes?

metric_definitions.via_in_pad, below_minimum, clearance_err: hard guards, no new breach versus baseline (decided 2026-10-18: no registration carries a hard guard the baseline already breaks): the arm's raw count minus the enhanced arm's raw count on the same row, floored at 0, so 0 in the enhanced arm by definition; the raw counts are reported as <name>_raw
metric_definitions.via_in_pad_raw: canary's via_in_pad.py on the graded board (canary rows: grade.sh's line)
metric_definitions.below_minimum_raw: KiCad track_width errors on the graded board
metric_definitions.clearance_errors_raw: KiCad error items of type clearance, hole_clearance, shorting_items, track_width, copper_edge_clearance and tracks_crossing, minus the same types on the unrouted input (demos and corpus; the canary inputs have none)
metric_definitions.power_layer_traces_raw: every trace on a power-type layer of the routed DSN: freerouting-dev power-traces {DSN} {SES}, the `all` count (0 expected under enhanced's power_layer_traces = none)
metric_definitions.drc_real: KiCad error-severity items other than unconnected items and starved thermals, minus the same types on the unrouted input; not worse than the enhanced arm
metric_definitions.inner_tracks: canary's inner_tracks.py count on the graded board (on canary every inner layer is a plane; on cm4-edge-ai-carrier inner signal layers count, so it is held to the enhanced arm's, not to 0); not worse than the enhanced arm
metric_definitions.kicad_unconnected: KiCad's unconnected items after importing the session
metric_definitions.unrouted: the router's final unrouted count (its log's last `final score: ... (N unrouted`)
metric_definitions.connections: the 'started with N unrouted' count of the route log (the corpus rows' default noise band)
metric_definitions.under_board_setup_mm: copper of the wide nets shipped under the net's Board Setup class width: freerouting-dev widths {WIDTHS_AGAINST} {SES} --json, the sum of under_mm over the nets whose class is wider than the board's narrowest class. The per-class delivered and under-width lengths of the wide classes (canary: Power_High, Switch_Node, Power, GND; interf_u and pic_programmer: their classes wider than 300 um; flight-computer-core-board: Ignitor; cm4-edge-ai-carrier: Power) from the same report, and the largest under-width nets, go in the done note
metric_definitions.wall_seconds: the route's wall time (date before and after the router process; the corpus rows: grade.sh's engine_seconds)
metric_definitions.aborted: 1 when the route was killed by its ulimit -v 8000000 or its timeout -k 10 1800, else 0

keep_rule: A candidate arm is accepted when (1) its pair passes freerouting-dev gate (no-regress totals: the kicad_unconnected total not worse than the enhanced arm's by more than the set's noise, no board worse than twice its band; every hard metric 0, i.e. no new breach versus the enhanced arm; drc_real and inner_tracks not worse than enhanced's on any row; no aborted route) and (2) either its kicad_unconnected total beats the enhanced arm's by more than the set's noise, or under_board_setup_mm summed over all rows is lower than the enhanced arm's (Q17's decision: beat the retry on unconnected, or tie it and narrow less copper). When both candidates are accepted, the one with the lower kicad_unconnected total is chosen; on equal totals the lower summed under_board_setup_mm; then the lower summed wall_seconds

decision_table.widen-back accepted: N05 adds router.neck_down.widen_back = true to ENHANCED (settings/profile.rs) with this measurement, a DIVERGENCES 'Profile enhanced' line and the profile test; the retry at 300 stays
decision_table.bounded-neck-widen-back accepted: N05 makes bounded-neck enhanced's neck-down (router.special.neck_down = bounded-neck, router.neck_down.widen_back = true) in place of the retry, with a DIVERGENCES 'Profile enhanced' line; router.neck_width_um stays as an option (Java's own setting) and leaves ENHANCED
decision_table.neither accepted: enhanced stays as it is; the numbers go in Q17.4's note; both stages stay opt-in (N02's keep-or-delete rule applied there)

stop_rule: one registered run per arm per row; no reruns with other settings, neck widths or neck distances; an aborted route is recorded (aborted = 1) and not rerun, and an arm with an aborted route is not accepted under this registration
run_limits: decided 2026-10-20: measurement runs stay short, never an hour in total; canary-pwr's two rows are kept, every other row routes in well under a minute by the earlier summaries (time_before), and the arm count is three. Expected route time per arm: about 7 min (9511d9a) + 1.8 min (plugin45) + under 40 s for the four other rows; about 29 min over the three arms, grading extra. Each route runs alone, under ulimit -v 8000000 and timeout -k 10 1800
memory_cap: ulimit -v 8000000 (8 GB of address space) on every route
not_registered: the arm bounded-neck without the widen-back, which Q17.4's list names: cut to keep the run short (run_limits). It differs from bounded-neck-widen-back only inside the neck zones, where bounded-neck alone keeps the neck and the widen-back widens what fits, so bounded-neck-widen-back is the stage as Q02 designed it (bounded neck plus piecewise widen-back with taper); a later registration may measure bounded-neck alone
router.neck_down.path_mm (KRT's fixed 2.5 mm neck length) and other neck widths
the plugin's canary export at a later canary commit: plugin45's stored DSN is the plugin row, as in N05.3
